title: 2014 AMC 10A Problem 20
statement: The product \((8)(888\dots8),\) where the second factor has \(k\) digits, is an integer whose digits have a sum of \(1000.\) What is \(k?\)

solutions.text:
The \(k\)-digit number made entirely of \(8\)s is \(8\frac{10^k-1}{9}\), so the product is \[ \begin{aligned} 64\frac{10^k-1}{9} &=7\cdot10^k\\ &\quad+100\frac{10^{k-2}-1}{9}\\ &\quad+4. \end{aligned} \] For \(k\ge2\), this is the number whose digits are \(7\), followed by \(k-2\) ones, then \(0,4\).

This means that for any \(k \geq 3,\) the sum of the digits in the product is \[ 7 + 4 + 0 + k - 2 = k + 9. \]

Finally, we get \[ k + 9 = 1000 \]\[ k = 991. \]

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Multiply a few examples to see the digit pattern
For \(k\ge3\), the product has \(k-2\) digits equal to \(1\)
